name: ICM7555IBAZ-T
title: ICM7555 single and ICM7556 dual general-purpose CMOS timers
summary: The ICM7555 is a CMOS version of the 555 RC timer, and the ICM7556 puts two of them in one package with shared supply and ground. They run from 2 V to 18 V on 60 µA (120 µA for the dual), their inputs draw picoamps and they reach 1 MHz, and in most circuits they replace a bipolar SE/NE 555/556 directly, usually without its supply and control-voltage capacitors. ICM7555IBAZ-T is the single timer in 8-lead SOIC for -25 °C to +85 °C, on tape and reel.
key_figures: 40 µA typ, 200 µA max at VDD = 5 V
80 µA typ, 400 µA max at VDD = 5 V

notes: All are Pb-free (RoHS compliant). C parts are rated 0 °C to +70 °C, I parts -25 °C to +85 °C.

pins.package: ICM7555, 8 Ld SOIC and 8 Ld PDIP

pins.name: TRIGGER
pins.function: Active-low trigger. Taking it below 1/3 of the supply sets the flip-flop: the output goes high and the discharge transistor turns off.

pins.name: OUTPUT
pins.function: Timer output from a CMOS inverter stage, swinging between the rails.

pins.name: RESET
pins.function: Active-low reset. Low forces the output low and the discharge transistor on, whatever the other inputs do.

pins.name: CONTROL VOLTAGE
pins.function: Tap on the internal divider at 2/3 of the supply, the threshold comparator's reference. A voltage forced on this pin moves both trip points. It needs no capacitor for stable operation.

pins.name: THRESHOLD
pins.function: Rising past 2/3 of the supply (with TRIGGER above 1/3) resets the flip-flop: output low, discharge on.

pins.name: DISCHARGE
pins.function: Drain of an n-channel transistor to GND. On while the output is low, off while it is high; it empties the timing capacitor.

pins.name: CONTROL VOLTAGE1
pins.function: Timer 1 control voltage, the 2/3 VDD divider tap.

pins.name: CONTROL VOLTAGE2
pins.function: Timer 2 control voltage, the 2/3 VDD divider tap.

circuits.title: Astable oscillator, one resistor
circuits.description: A square-wave oscillator from one resistor and one capacitor. R runs from OUTPUT back to the timing node, where C, TRIGGER and THRESHOLD meet: with the output high C charges through R up to 2/3 VDD, the output falls and C discharges through R down to 1/3 VDD, and the cycle repeats, giving f = 1/(1.4 RC) at 50 % duty. DISCHARGE, unused by the timing, switches in step with the output and with a 10k pull-up to VDD gives a second, open-drain output. RESET sits at VDD. The capacitor on CONTROL VOLTAGE is optional.

circuits.title: Astable oscillator, two resistors
circuits.description: The classic two-resistor astable. C charges from VDD through RA and RB in series and discharges through RB alone into DISCHARGE; TRIGGER and THRESHOLD both watch the capacitor. Frequency is 1.44/((RA + 2RB)C) and the duty cycle (RA + RB)/(RA + 2RB), so RA and RB set the duty cycle. RESET is held at VDD; the capacitor on CONTROL VOLTAGE is optional.

circuits.title: Monostable (one-shot)
circuits.description: A one-shot. Between pulses DISCHARGE holds C empty and the output is low. A falling edge on TRIGGER sets the flip-flop: the output goes high and C charges from VDD through RA. When C reaches 2/3 VDD at THRESHOLD the flip-flop resets, DISCHARGE empties C and the output falls, so the pulse lasts 1.1 RA C. RESET is brought out as an active-low input. VDD is at most 18 V; the capacitor on CONTROL VOLTAGE is optional.

operation.text: CMOS RC timers that drop into most SE/NE 555/556 and 355 sockets, and match the TLC555/556 in most cases. The ICM7556 holds two ICM7555 timers that run independently and share only V+ and GND. Both work as astable oscillators and monostable one-shots, with timing from microseconds to hours.

Supply current is low (ICM7555 60 µA, ICM7556 120 µA), the Threshold, Trigger and Reset inputs draw about 20 pA, the supply range is 2 V to 18 V, operation reaches 1 MHz and temperature stability is 0.005 %/°C at +25 °C. The supply is not crowbarred while the output switches. Because the inputs draw so little, timing resistors can be larger than a bipolar 555 allows, for longer time constants. Both edges of the output have small offsets from the rails.

An output transition draws a supply current spike of 2 mA to 3 mA, compared with 300 mA to 400 mA for a bipolar 555, so the supply normally needs no decoupling capacitor. The on-chip comparators are CMOS with very high input impedance, so in most cases the Control Voltage pin needs no capacitor either. An ICM7555 design typically saves two capacitors, an ICM7556 design three.
The timer itself draws little, but the timing network can draw much more; high R and low C keep the total down in the astable and monostable circuits.
The output stage is a CMOS inverter. Into CMOS loads it swings to both rails at any supply voltage. From 4.5 V upward it drives at least two standard TTL loads.

With the output feeding the timing capacitor through one resistor, the timer triggers itself and free-runs. The output swings rail to rail as a square wave of 50 % duty cycle, with symmetrical trip points and output swings. Frequency moves by under 1 % across a 5 V to 15 V supply.

As a one-shot, the timer holds the timing capacitor discharged through its internal transistor while idle. A negative-going pulse on TRIGGER (pin 2) sets the flip-flop, releasing the capacitor and driving OUTPUT high. The capacitor then charges exponentially with time constant RA C; at 2/3 V+ the threshold comparator resets the flip-flop, the capacitor is discharged quickly and OUTPUT goes low. OUTPUT cannot fall while TRIGGER is still low.

CONTROL VOLTAGE sets the trip voltages of both the threshold and the trigger comparator. Driving it frequency-modulates an astable, or stops it oscillating, depending on the level; in a monostable it changes the delay time.

RESET trips at about the same level as on the bipolar 555/556, 0.6 V to 0.7 V, and is a very high impedance at every supply voltage. It acts only on the internal flip-flop, which sets OUTPUT and DISCHARGE together, so a slowly falling reset edge does not give the multiple-threshold trouble seen on bipolar parts.
Both trigger and reset act on falling (negative-going) edges.
Inputs that are not used are to be tied down.
The three resistors of the trip-point divider are each 100 kΩ ±20 % typical.

A -T suffix is tape and reel of 2,500 (reel details in TB347). All listed parts are Pb-free with a 100 % matte tin plus anneal (e3) finish, solderable with SnPb or Pb-free processes; moisture sensitivity is classified at Pb-free reflow peak temperatures to IPC/JEDEC J-STD-020 (MSL on the product page, TB363).
